label: Ch 5 · Your playlist and your focus

scenes.title: Your playlist and your focus
scenes.say: Chapter five. What your playlist is doing to your focus, and to your daydreams.
A recall from chapter four. In the job-seeker study, what did the most positive fantasies predict two years later?
scenes.sayA: Fewer applications, fewer job offers, and lower salaries.
scenes.a: Fewer applications, fewer offers, lower salaries

scenes.text: No published study tests phonk, hardstyle, jumpstyle, slowed + reverb, sped-up songs or TikTok audios directly. Genre claims are *inferred* from research on ~lyrics, tempo, loudness and emotion~.
scenes.say: One honest note first. No published study tests phonk, hardstyle, jumpstyle, slowed and reverb edits, sped-up songs or TikTok audios directly. Everything genre-specific here is inferred from research on lyrics, tempo, loudness and emotion.

scenes.head: How much background music hurts, by task
scenes.say: The headline average is misleading. Across studies, background music versus silence shows essentially no overall effect, because harm to reading and memory cancels out benefits to mood and sport. Look at the task and the picture sharpens. Across 65 studies, music with lyrics harmed reading comprehension by about a third of a standard deviation, as much as background speech. Lyrics also cut verbal recall. Instrumental music was roughly neutral.

scenes.bigl: out of 100: how distracting people rated their favourite songs
scenes.text: Liking the music *does not protect you*. Favourite lyrical songs were ~as disruptive~ as songs people disliked.
scenes.say: Liking the music does not protect you. In one study, people's own favourite songs with lyrics were as disruptive as music they disliked. They rated their favourites 75 out of 100 for distraction, against 10 for quiet.

scenes.head: Two ways sound breaks your thinking
items: Changing sound (beats, syllables, melodic jumps) breaks holding things in order
Words you understand compete with any task about meaning
Rap hits both: dense, fast, understandable lyrics. Worst case for scriptwriting.
scenes.say: There are two separate mechanisms. First, any sound that changes moment to moment, like beats, syllables and melodic jumps, disrupts tasks that need you to hold things in order in your head. Second, words you understand compete with any task involving meaning. Rap, with dense, fast, understandable lyrics in your own language, hits both at once. That makes scriptwriting its worst-case task. Introverts are more impaired than extraverts.

scenes.head: Tempo and loudness
scenes.text: When instrumental music varied in speed and volume, *only fast and loud* pushed reading comprehension ~below baseline~.
scenes.note: Your genres sit squarely in that corner
scenes.say: Tempo and loudness matter even without lyrics. When instrumental music was varied by speed and volume, only the fast and loud combination pushed reading comprehension below baseline. Your genres sit squarely in that corner.

scenes.head: Your genres, by tempo (beats per minute)
scenes.say: Hardstyle is typically produced around 150 beats per minute, with overdriven, hard kick drums. Jumpstyle runs 140 to 150. Drift and gym phonk run about 140 to 170, with distorted bass and cowbell rolls, and gym phonk is built for maximum aggression. Sped-up edits play songs about 35 percent faster.

scenes.head: Creative work is not an exception

items: Finding the one right answer, like the right hook
All music impaired it, vs quiet
Upbeat instrumental helped loose brainstorming (1 study)
Preferred music cut mind-wandering on dull, easy tasks

scenes.say: Creative work is not an exception. On insight problems, where you need the one right answer, like choosing the right hook, music with familiar lyrics, foreign lyrics or no lyrics all impaired performance compared with quiet, even for people who habitually study with music. There are two narrow exceptions. Upbeat instrumental music raised creativity during loose brainstorming in one study. And preferred music reduced mind-wandering on a dull, easy task, in people used to background music. The authors warn this is not tested on complex tasks. And a meta-analysis that found a small benefit drew mostly on music heard before the task, and on classical music.

scenes.bigl: more vivid imagined scenes with music
scenes.text: Music does more than distract. It *drives imagination*, and changes the ~emotional tone and content~ of what you imagine.
scenes.say: Music does more than distract. It drives imagination. In a directed imagery task, every music condition made imagined journeys about 2.7 times more vivid than silence, and changed their emotional tone and content.

scenes.head: Different music, different daydreams
scenes.say: In a study of 62 people, heroic music produced mind-wandering that was far more positive and exciting than sad music, full of empowering thoughts. Only about 2 percent of the thoughts involved logical reasoning. Sad music, by contrast, produced more mind-wandering than happy music, of an inward, self-focused, emotional kind.

scenes.bigl: people with MD: music deepens the daydream
scenes.text: I can keep myself from daydreaming so long as I maintain concentration, but *in the presence of music, that becomes difficult*.
scenes.say: The only dedicated study of music in MD interviewed 41 people. In 36 of them, the dominant theme was that music enhances the experience. They described exactly your work-session problem. I can keep myself from daydreaming so long as I maintain concentration, but in the presence of music, that becomes difficult. Another said: it's harder to come out if I'm listening to music. I can continue for hours. Music even sets the pace of the plot, with characters fighting to the beat, and it drives the urge to pace around.

scenes.head: Music does four jobs in MD
scenes.say: Somer concludes that music does four jobs. It distances you from external reality, triggers complex visual storylines, deepens absorption, and intensifies the fantasy through emotion. He calls the relationship potentially addictive, and recommends stimulus control: controlling exposure to the cue itself. A 2026 preprint adds that music was reported as the most effective tool for triggering and maintaining daydreams.

scenes.head: Your playlist, part by part
items: Rap: worst for scripting; supplies story and identity material
Phonk: fast, loud, ‘heroic’: cues power fantasies and pacing
Hardstyle, jumpstyle: fast and loud: action fantasies
Sped-up: adds speed to every lyric problem
Slowed + reverb: sad, nostalgic, inward: likely most fantasy-inducing
TikTok audios: short loops, earworms that follow you into silence
scenes.say: Here is your playlist, part by part, as inference. Rap is worst for scripting, and supplies story and identity material. Phonk is fast, loud and close to heroic music, so it cues empowering, self-as-hero fantasies and the urge to pace. Hardstyle and jumpstyle are fast and loud, which invites movement and action fantasies. Sped-up edits add speed to every lyric problem. Slowed and reverb edits are less arousing, but sad music increases inward mind-wandering, so they are plausibly the most fantasy-inducing part of the library. And TikTok audios are short loops, which create earworms that follow you into silent work.

scenes.head: Slowed + reverb: ‘false nostalgia’
scenes.text: People might be very bored or sad… They find their *escape* in slowed songs.
scenes.note: Sped-up hashtags: 11+ billion views, built to ‘suck you in’
scenes.say: Slowed and reverb deserves a special note, because it can pass for study music. Producers describe it as false nostalgia, with listeners mourning parties they never attended. One creator explains its appeal: people might be very bored or sad. They find their escape in slowed songs. That is close to a description of daydream fuel. And sped-up songs were engineered for capture. As one social media manager put it, you get immediately sucked in, and don't have time to think. Their hashtags have drawn more than 11 billion views.

scenes.head: Earworms
scenes.text: Repetition causes them: after hearing a chorus up to 4 times, *68 percent* had an earworm the next day, and ~working memory~ suffered even after the music stopped.
scenes.note: Chewing gum reduced earworms in a lab test
scenes.say: About 90 percent of people get earworms at least weekly, and heavy listeners get them more. Recent, repeated exposure is the main trigger, and mind-wandering is another, so MD and earworms feed each other. In one experiment, hearing a chorus up to four times produced earworms in 68 percent of people the next day, and more exposure meant more interference with working memory, even after the music had stopped. Chewing gum, which occupies the inner voice, reduced earworms in a lab test. And listening near bedtime is linked to sleep-disrupting earworms.

scenes.bigl: men chose an electric shock over sitting alone with their thoughts
scenes.text: Expect *withdrawal* when you switch to silence. People with MD describe no music as ~an itch you cannot scratch~.
scenes.note: A predictable transition, not proof that silence fails
scenes.say: Expect withdrawal when you switch to silence. Across 11 studies, many people found just 6 to 15 minutes alone with their thoughts unpleasant. In one, 12 of 18 men gave themselves an electric shock rather than sit quietly, though critics debate what that means. People with MD describe the absence of music as like having an itch you cannot scratch. No study has measured how long it takes for silence to feel normal. The early discomfort is a predictable transition, not evidence that silence works worse. And your own sense of what helps is unreliable: people believe their favourite music helps, even while it measurably impairs them.

scenes.head: Silence and its alternatives
items: Silence: the benchmark for reading, writing and creativity
White or pink noise: slightly helps ADHD (g = +0.25), slightly hurts others (g = −0.21)
Nature sounds: beat city sounds for attention. Good between blocks.
scenes.say: So what instead? Across the main studies, quiet matches or beats lyrical music for reading, verbal memory and creativity. White and pink noise slightly helped young people with ADHD or high inattention, but slightly hurt people without it, and the volume needs watching to protect hearing. Brown noise has no controlled studies. Natural soundscapes beat city soundscapes on an attention test, which suits recovery between work blocks. Steady sound has no melody, lyrics or emotional imagery, so it makes a reasonable bridge while silence still feels uncomfortable.

scenes.head: Task by sound
items: Scripting, outlining, reading: silence. Bridge: low pink noise or rain.
Loose brainstorming: silence or a walk
Mechanical editing: silence or steady noise. No music.
Breaks: a walk without audio, not short audios
scenes.say: Here is the task-by-sound plan. For scripting, outlining and reading: silence, with low pink noise or rain only as a bridge. For choosing hooks and angles, and for AI prompting: silence. For loose brainstorming: silence, or a walk. For mechanical editing: silence or steady noise, but not music, because for you its role as a trigger outweighs any arousal benefit. And for breaks: a walk without audio, not scrolling short audios that reload earworms and fantasy cues.

scenes.text: Want the energy boost without the cue? A *brisk walk* before work: short exercise improves memory.
scenes.note: The evidence points where your values already point: silence for focused work
scenes.say: The research offers one thing you can use without music. A short burst of arousal before a task helps performance, and a brisk walk delivers it too: short bouts of exercise improve memory. Nobody has tested whether vocal audio without instruments behaves like music in MD. Researchers locate music's pull in pleasure and emotional absorption, which argues for caution with any emotionally evocative audio during focused work. On every point where the evidence is clear, it points where your values already point: silence for focused work.
Why doesn't liking a song protect your focus?
scenes.sayA: Because the harm comes from changing sound and understandable words, not from how much you like it. Favourite lyrical songs were as disruptive as disliked ones.
scenes.a: The harm comes from changing sound and words, not liking. Favourites disrupted just as much.

scenes.say: Which part of your playlist is plausibly the most fantasy-inducing, and why?
scenes.sayA: Slowed and reverb. It is sad-leaning and nostalgic, and sad music increases inward, emotional mind-wandering.
scenes.a: Slowed + reverb: sad, nostalgic music increases inward mind-wandering
